answer: The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 35 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. Because the vertex hash is checked against the island checkpoint at intake, the prism audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm of 1309 identities would post 2465 proofs and burn roughly 46 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
